mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 0.5% signals the onset of monetary tightening, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.5%, or the Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicate a strengthening labor market, boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with PAYEMS growth and UNRATE decline, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion, a decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening residential demand, which is a leading indicator of economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods during late-cycle expansion with HOUST decline, or the Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO) indicates expanding manufacturing output, which correlates with stronger corporate profits and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO rises, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1100 thousand units signals weakening residential demand, which is a leading indicator of economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 45% of periods when HOUST falls below 1100, or the Rank IC remains below 0.01 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 235 and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) remains below 0.3%, the market perceives persistent inflation without policy response, eroding real returns and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of periods meeting the trigger condition, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-unemployment recovery phase, a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals improving labor market conditions, boosting consumer confidence and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods during high-unemployment recovery with UNRATE decline, or the Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.
